headline: This year we’ve had a clear jump in model capability where instead of telling agents precisely what to do, it’s better to use these systems to solve problems you can’t easily define yourself. A year ago you’d need to very clearly tell agents the how to design and develop your product idea, or there was almost no chance of success. Now, increasingly, the agent likely can come up with a better implementation than you’d have thought of because you can have it connect the dots between a far greater solution space than you can. This will be increasingly true in basically every domain of kneeler work. We’re going to see this impact in finance, legal, life sciences, cyber, and many other spaces where no person can hold onto all the available relevant industry knowledge to think of the best solution. Ultimately this is going to reshape our relationship with AI and how we deploy agents in our work. It won’t be about explicitly telling them, but instead giving them goals and enough freedom to pursue them in the best way they can.

headline: Here's my new video testing GPT-Astra 6.2 head to head against Gemini 4 and Fable 5.2 across 5 use cases. I tried all 3 last night for video, game, design, writing, and holding their ground when I push back. Surprisingly, Fable did NOT win on everything. 📌 Watch the full breakdown now: https://t.co/ePailW82Zs Quick review of GPT Astra and Gemini Carbon: 1. Astra feels lazy next to Fable and Carbon. It did an incomplete analysis of my YouTube stats and wrote an off-topic essay. OpenAI models "had that dog in them" in the 5.6 days, but don't seem to anymore. On the plus side, its design taste has improved. 2. Carbon really impressed me with its writing. But it's slow and needs work on design and 3D (it stuffs the UX with too much info). Still, it works harder and feels smarter than Astra. As for Fable 5.2, well it's still the best overall and kept surprising me with its creativity, as you'll see in the video. Watch it and let me know what you think in the replies!
